subject: Privacy Addendum Q&A: controller vs processor & subprocessors
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@finlytics.com>, Gavin Cho <gcho@finlytics.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 15:05:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps on DPA questions

Hi Elena / Gavin —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on the privacy items you raised: 

1) Controller vs Processor: you asked us to clarify where Redwood sits in the stack. Short answer: Redwood is the processor for inference and telemetry data; customers are the controller for any data they ingest and the decisions made using outputs. We can provide contractual language that maps specific data flows; I flagged that for legal.

2) Subprocessors: you requested the current subprocessors list and a process for notification if we add critical infra providers. We have a published list and an SLA for notice on critical additions — I’ll attach the DPA and subprocessors link.

3) Breach notice & timeline: you asked how we handle incidents involving customer data and expected notification windows. We typically commit to notification within 72 hours for incidents that materially affect customer data; legal can confirm exact wording and exceptions.

4) Data residency & retention: you mentioned a regulatory requirement to keep data in the EU for certain workflows. Redwood supports region pinning for inference and can offer EU-only footprints for this account. We also have configurable logging retention (default 30 days for operational logs) and options for customer-managed retention.

Next steps I propose: 
- I’ll loop in our legal lead to answer DPA wording questions and share a redlined DPA (marissa).
- Please add any specific redlines to the attached spreadsheet (FinLytics_DPA_Questions.xlsx) and we’ll prioritize responses.
- If acceptable, we can set up a short legal-to-legal call (30 min) early next week.

Attachments: FinLytics_DPA_Questions.xlsx (template for mapping asks)

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0148

From: Elena Morales <elena@finlytics.com>

Cc: Gavin Cho <gcho@finlytics.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 17:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps on DPA questions

Thanks, Jonas — very helpful summary. A couple of clarifying questions from our privacy/legal team that came up while reviewing notes: 

- Can Redwood confirm whether customer-provided data used for model tuning (if we choose to) is explicitly excluded from any internal model training? We need explicit contractual guarantees there.
- For subprocessors: will FinLytics receive advance notice (e.g., 30 days) for any additions that process customer content? Also need a callable process to object to a subprocessor on reasonable grounds.
- Breach notice: 72 hours is acceptable as a target, but can you confirm whether that includes notification of suspected incidents or only confirmed incidents with impact analysis? Our counsel prefers early notice for suspected incidents.
- Logs & PII: can Redwood provide details on what logs are stored by default (request metadata vs full payloads), and whether PII in logs is redacted by default? We have strict retention rules for raw PII.

I’m attaching a short list of redlines from our side (we’ll put the formal spreadsheet in the shared doc). Happy to do legal-to-legal if that helps.

Kind regards,
Elena Morales
Head of Privacy, FinLytics
elena@finlytics.com

Hi Elena / Gavin —

Thanks for the clear questions. I’ve addressed each point below and attached our DPA template (Redwood_DPA_v2.pdf) plus a filled example of how the contract maps to your asks (FinLytics_DPA_Questions.xlsx). Please note these are our standard positions; we’re happy to negotiate specific redlines where needed.

1) Model training & customer data: Redwood does not use customer-provided content for internal model training or to improve any shared models unless you explicitly opt in via a separate agreement and a controlled process. We can add a clear exclusion clause in Section 3.2 of the DPA that prevents use of customer data for model training without written consent. 

2) Subprocessors & notice: We publish our subprocessors list at the link below and commit to providing 30 days’ notice for additions that will process customer content. For critical infra changes, we provide advance notice and a description of the change. The DPA includes a reasonable objection right — objecting parties can propose mitigation or suspension of processing until resolved. Link: https://app.redwood.com/subprocessors-list

3) Breach notice & suspected incidents: Our standard is notification of confirmed incidents that materially affect customer data within 72 hours of becoming aware. However, we recognize your preference for early notice of suspected incidents; we can include a contractual commitment to notify of suspected incidents "as soon as reasonably practicable" and to provide interim updates while the investigation is underway. We’ll include language about timelines for initial notification and follow-up reports.

4) Logs, PII, and retention: Default behavior:
- Operational logs: request metadata (timestamp, model version, request size), request and response identifiers; default retention 30 days.
- Optional request payload storage: by default we do not persist raw payloads beyond what is required for caching and KV stores; persistence and retention are configurable per account.
- PII: we do not automatically redact PII from payloads; instead we offer configurable redaction/tokenization features and recommendations to shield sensitive fields at ingestion. We can add contractual representations that Redwood will support redaction workflows and that customers can opt for automatic redaction for specified fields.

5) Data residency: Redwood supports regional model pinning and EU-only inference for customers who require EU residency. We can add a Data Residency Schedule to the DPA specifying which processing locations are in scope.

6) Evidence & compliance materials: We can provide SOC 2 Type II summary, security whitepaper, and a scoped audit report on request under an NDA.

Next steps: 
- I attached Redwood_DPA_v2.pdf with the clauses called out.
- Please add your redlines to FinLytics_DPA_Questions.xlsx and return to me; I’ll coordinate redline resolution and prepare a short legal-to-legal call if helpful.
- For signature we typically use DocuSign; provisional link: https://docusign.com/xyz123456789 (we’ll generate a case-specific envelope once redlines are agreed).

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v2.pdf (DPA template, 24 pages), FinLytics_DPA_Questions.xlsx (your questions mapped)

If you prefer, we can schedule a 30 minute call Mon/Tue next week — I’m available Tue 9–11am PST.
